text:
Quinn Hughes is playing more than 28 minutes a night for Minnesota and making the most of them: 26 points in 19 games, an eight-game point streak, and 10 power-play points. Evolving-Hockey rated him the most valuable defenseman in the league last season, 1st among 215 with 4.9 wins above replacement, in the season Vancouver traded him to the Wild.

There's a contract clock too. Daily Faceoff's look at the 2027 free-agent class asked the question hanging over the Wild's season: "Does Quinn Hughes make it to market?"

The play underneath is real. Minnesota gets 58% of the expected goals (the share of chance quality) with him at five on five, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 99th percentile among defensemen for primary shot assists last season. The number to discount is the goals: 6 on 3.5 expected, shooting 12% after 4% last season. Expect fewer goals; the assists aren't going anywhere. His ice time has climbed to about 29 and a half minutes a night over his last ten games, which tells you how much the Wild lean on him.
headline: Quinn Hughes, a contract year and a best-in-class start
